facts.statement: The research was a single-site feasibility trial carried out in a French outpatient chemotherapy clinic.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The study included adult women diagnosed with breast cancer who did not have brain metastases or medical reasons to avoid virtual reality.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Nurses provided virtual reality sessions during four back-to-back chemotherapy appointments, and the women chose whether to participate.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: A total of 217 virtual reality sessions were made available to 60 women, whose median age was 51.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: About 63% of the participants agreed to use the virtual reality headset for at least three out of the four chemotherapy visits.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The women reported low levels of simulator sickness, high satisfaction with the experience, and 91% said they would do it again.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Nurses expressed less desire to use the technology regularly because it increased their workload.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The authors state that further clinical trials are required to determine how virtual reality affects patient well-being during treatment.
facts.subject: humans
